decisions.processing_scope: App Store distribution, StoreKit billing and developer account administration; no raw app memo body is established in this flow.

dpa.assessment: Existing September 1 human review found no separate developer DPA for ordinary App Store billing; Apple acts on its own end-user relationship.
dpa.action: Preserve the accepted review; assess any additional Apple data-processing product separately.

data_use.assessment: Store purchase/download records have independent purposes and long financial retention; owner review leaves provider-detail questions open.
data_use.action: Do not promise deletion of Apple purchase records through a SimpleMemo account deletion.

sla.assessment: A numeric developer-facing App Store SLA and remedy were not established.
sla.action: Budget operationally for interruption; do not quote an uptime entitlement.

exit.assessment: An iOS app cannot replace App Store distribution with an equivalent provider. Existing reports and source copies preserve only part of the business.
exit.action: Before termination preserve financial/release records and check transfer eligibility; do not cancel solely to raise coverage.

conditions: Retain the existing App Store/StoreKit use and owner acceptance.
Account transfer or product expansion requires a new review.
unresolved: Developer-facing incident deadline, named processor scope and account-specific remedies remain unknown.

decisions.processing_scope: Workers processes memo recipient, subject and body; D1 stores inquiry content; Pages, KV and the domain have distinct roles.

dpa.assessment: The account describes standard DPA incorporation; v6.4 and Self-Serve section 6.1 were reviewed, but historic/custom agreement scope is unresolved.
dpa.action: Continue the existing services with that uncertainty recorded; do not assert a negotiated or signed contract.

data_use.assessment: Personal data is processed. D1 APAC placement does not establish Japan-only storage; service-specific subprocessors and purpose limits apply.
data_use.action: Keep existing retention/access controls and narrowly scoped deployment credentials; review any new data destination.

sla.assessment: Workers runtime and Enterprise SLAs do not establish D1, KV or Pages coverage. Actual remedy eligibility remains unresolved.
sla.action: Maintain separate service failure evidence and use the applicable claim window only after verifying entitlement.

exit.assessment: Local/schema restoration exercises and iOS Outbox do not prove a complete D1/KV migration or durable production recovery.
exit.action: Before provider termination export and restore required data on the replacement, validate idempotency and cutover, then revoke the old path.

conditions: Continue current Workers/Pages/KV/D1 use under existing controls.
Do not expand sensitive-data scope or claim complete failover without new evidence.
unresolved: Applicable accepted version, per-service SLA, storage/access geography, production backup and full restoration remain unverified.

decisions.processing_scope: Memo, authentication and lifecycle email delivery; addresses, subject and body are processed.

dpa.assessment: A signed DPA dated 2025-12-31 was observed; later public HTML has not been proved to replace it. Human acceptance on September 1 remains historical.
dpa.action: Retain that acceptance and reconcile the executed text before relying on a later deletion or liability clause.

data_use.assessment: The ordinary plan has purpose limits but not the Enterprise express training ban. Data fields sent to Anthropic/RunPod remain unknown.
data_use.action: Continue the owner-accepted risk; retain overages disabled and do not enable additional AI or storage features by inference.

sla.assessment: The observed Pro plan does not establish Enterprise 99.99% entitlement or a monetary remedy.
sla.action: Plan for sender interruption using existing retry/dead-letter handling.

exit.assessment: CSV/API export and public deletion wording are distinct from migration of delivery state and sender reputation; no alternative sender is proven.
exit.action: Before termination preserve necessary delivery records, verify the executed deletion term, and test new DNS/sender/idempotency handling.

conditions: Preserve the September 1 accept-as-is decision and observed Pro configuration.
Any paid storage option or sender replacement needs its own scoped decision.
unresolved: Signed/public DPA reconciliation, AI subprocessor data fields and a complete sender migration remain unresolved.

decisions.processing_scope: Existing operator AI workflows may process code, prompts and author/account metadata. The legacy app-data none label does not cover all operator inputs.

dpa.assessment: Commercial DPA sections and annexes were read; they do not automatically cover a consumer Pro/Max or every historical Claude route.
dpa.action: Treat account-specific coverage as unknown and keep credentials and unnecessary personal data out of prompts.

data_use.assessment: Commercial processor instructions, breach and deletion terms were reviewed; subprocessors and actual model-routing scope differ by product.
data_use.action: Use bounded existing inputs; no model-training or third-party sharing expansion is authorized by this review.

sla.assessment: Published support tiers do not establish a numeric uptime commitment for the observed accounts.
sla.action: Retain rate-limit/failure handling and do not describe support response as uptime insurance.

exit.assessment: The old primary Claude schedule is manual-only. Actual Codex replacement observations now exist, but other model/QA callers and data export are outside that proof.
exit.action: Preserve prompts and source; assess all remaining callers and export/delete required provider data before complete termination.

conditions: Keep the old schedule stopped and the existing Codex replacement in place.
Retain separate account/input reviews for other Claude routes.
unresolved: Consumer versus commercial entitlement, SCC/UK incorporated text, full historical data deletion and all alternative callers remain unverified.

decisions.processing_scope: Observed BigQuery Search Console exports and aggregates; a customer-level app funnel warehouse is not established.

dpa.assessment: The reviewed Cloud DPA is the relevant candidate for covered BigQuery processing; account assent and overrides are not fully established.
dpa.action: Retain Cloud and Search Console as separate contractual services.

data_use.assessment: Current evidence is search-export data. Export storage can grow indefinitely without partition expiration; actual expiration/region were not verified.
data_use.action: Keep query scopes bounded and check expiration/region before collecting additional data classes.

sla.assessment: BigQuery Standard and other editions have different SLOs; data transfer timing does not guarantee upstream Search Console completeness.
sla.action: Do not select an entitlement by assumption; retain request/backoff evidence and verify the edition before a claim.

exit.assessment: Stored aggregates preserve observations, but no complete dataset export and non-Google restore is proven.
exit.action: Before deletion/export termination preserve schema, date partitions and required history; prove count/date integrity in the replacement.

conditions: Continue the observed search-export workload.
Do not describe this as completed app-level financial/cohort integration.
unresolved: Edition, accepted contract, region, retention settings and complete export/restore remain unverified.

decisions.processing_scope: Search property administration and retrieval of search queries, impressions, clicks and position aggregates.

dpa.assessment: The reviewed Japan-country Google general terms are separate from GCP. A Search Console processor DPA has not been established.
dpa.action: Do not use the Cloud DPA as proof for the upstream search service.

data_use.assessment: Queries and property metrics are exported to a billed Cloud project; observed aggregation is not individual app behavior.
data_use.action: Keep retrieval to the owned property and avoid asserting person-level attribution.

sla.assessment: Setup timing and retry guidance do not create a contractual data-delivery SLA for Search Console.
sla.action: Represent late/missing data as missing and preserve last verified observations.

exit.assessment: BigQuery exports and snapshots preserve a limited date range; they cannot recreate unavailable upstream observations.
exit.action: Before disconnecting preserve the required historical reports and remove export/access grants after verification.

conditions: Retain read-only owned-property observation.
Use missing-data semantics in reports.
unresolved: Search-specific DPA/remedies, actual account terms and complete historical portability remain unverified.

decisions.processing_scope: Firebase Authentication and App Check; Google/Apple sign-in code can provide email/name. App Check and OAuth are separate paths.

dpa.assessment: The Firebase service list places Auth/App Check under GCP terms; the Cloud DPA and appendices were read. Actual accepted version and overrides remain unresolved.
dpa.action: Continue existing authentication with the Cloud/Firebase scope recorded; do not infer acceptance from the Blaze label.

data_use.assessment: Personal data is processed. Service Data sharing is distinct from auth customer data; subprocessors and region are not fully mapped.
data_use.action: Do not interpret the sharing toggle as consent to train on customer authentication data; review added scopes separately.

sla.assessment: Ordinary Firebase Auth lacks the enterprise SLA; Blaze does not prove Identity Platform upgrade. Its SLA covers specified requests, not every sign-in/App Check flow.
sla.action: Do not promise 99.95% for the full authentication flow; verify the upgrade before relying on remedies.

exit.assessment: OAuth disable returns 503; it does not bypass authentication or stop every App Check request. Equivalent migration is untested.
exit.action: Before replacing authentication prove user mapping, reauthentication, token validation and rollback; preserve fail-closed behavior.

conditions: Continue existing Auth/App Check without bypassing verification.
Any new auth product, scopes or migration requires a fresh review.
unresolved: Actual DPA acceptance, Identity Platform upgrade, contacts, regional access, SCC and end-to-end migration are unresolved.

dpa.action: Retain the Welcome-plan observation and do not claim signed coverage.

data_use.assessment: Custom event filtering excludes memo text; it does not establish all SDK behavior. Optional AI subprocessors are not proof of opt-in.

sla.assessment: Link serving and APIs/reporting have different percentages and limited credits; applicability and meaningful remedy on Welcome are unknown.
sla.action: Do not use a paid-plan SLA as a recovery guarantee for the current plan.

exit.assessment: The event flag does not stop SDK start. Keychain identifiers may persist; DPA bulk-deletion wording is at least ninety days, not a maximum guarantee.
exit.action: Before exit implement/verify SDK-wide stop, identifier deletion and export, retaining the legal deletion exceptions.

conditions: Keep the current filtered event scope; prohibit new direct identifiers through this review.
Re-review before Welcome term end or any paid renewal.
unresolved: SDK-wide traffic/stop, consent, identifiers and deletion, customer DPA execution, renewal terms and migration are unresolved.
